business_problem: Growing mobile and fixed-network traffic makes manual planning and operations less responsive; Vodafone aims to anticipate demand, adapt network resources, and resolve issues before customers are affected.
solution_summary: Vodafone describes an in-house AI-for-networks program that combines digital-twin technology, AI-controlled radio capacity, and optimization of the User Plane Function (UPF). Environmental features and network-performance data are mapped alongside one another so engineers can test changes before applying them; operational performance data also supports earlier diagnosis and action. In a trial, an AI-controlled antenna shifts capacity between a shopping centre by day and nearby homes in the evening, replacing manual changes that took days with adjustments in 20 to 30 minutes. UPF optimization targets more efficient traffic routing, hardware use, and energy consumption. Vodafone coordinates network domains with specialized controllers close to radio, transport, fixed, and core networks, while L4S technology reduces end-to-end latency for AI applications. The page does not identify storage platforms, model vendors, or an end-to-end serving stack.
